title: From a useful idea to a published guide
description: Follow the explanation and its working artifact together. Explore how the brief shapes drafting, review, publication, and reuse.
footer: Fictional example. Replace the content and relationships with your own workflow.

plans.title: Publish a practical guide
plans.summary: Turn one reader question into a reviewed guide with a clear next action.

steps.title: Define the reader's decision
steps.description: Choose one reader and the decision the guide should help them make. A narrow brief gives drafting and review the same target.
steps.checkpoint: The reader, question, and useful outcome fit in three lines.

artifact.title: Editorial brief
artifact.code:
Reader: a first-time project contributor
Question: Which issue should I start with?
Useful outcome: select one bounded task and make a first contribution
Scope: issue labels, setup effort, and asking for context
Exclude: advanced architecture and release administration
artifact.note: This brief is the review reference, not a claim about an existing project.

steps.title: Draft around the decision
steps.description: Build the guide around the reader's choice. Give concrete examples and preserve unknowns instead of inventing project-specific facts.
steps.checkpoint: Each section helps the reader choose or begin a task.

artifact.title: Drafting prompt
artifact.code:
Use the editorial brief and the supplied project documentation.
Draft a guide that helps a new contributor select one issue.
Include: a comparison of task sizes, one worked choice,
a setup checklist, and the next action.
Mark missing facts as [VERIFY]. Do not invent commands or policies.

steps.title: Test the draft against the brief
steps.description: Check factual claims against the supplied documentation. Then ask whether a new contributor can make the intended decision without missing context.
steps.checkpoint: All verification markers are resolved or explicitly disclosed.

artifact.title: Review checklist
artifact.code:
[ ] The guide answers the brief's question
[ ] Setup steps match the current project docs
[ ] The worked example explains the tradeoff
[ ] Links point to the intended destination
[ ] No unresolved [VERIFY] markers remain
[ ] The next action is specific and achievable

steps.title: Package the guide for readers
steps.description: Publish the reviewed guide with a title that matches the reader's question. Check the public page in the same form the reader will see.
steps.checkpoint: The page is readable on a narrow screen and its next-action link works.

artifact.title: Publication record
artifact.code:
Title: Choose your first contribution
Summary: Compare candidate issues and pick one bounded task.
Reader action: open the contributor issue list
Owner: [editor]
Published URL: [add after publication]
Review again when: onboarding instructions or issue labels change
artifact.note: Fill in the record after publication; this example does not publish anything.

steps.title: Use reader feedback to revise
steps.description: Record where readers hesitate. Change the brief when the question was wrong, or the guide when its answer was incomplete.
steps.checkpoint: Each revision maps to a concrete observation.

artifact.title: Feedback-to-change note
artifact.code:
Observation: readers cannot estimate setup effort
Evidence: [link or anonymized feedback]
Affected decision: which issue is small enough to start
Proposed change: add setup-effort examples to the comparison
Check after revision: can a new reader explain the tradeoff?

plans.title: Adapt a guide for another channel
plans.summary: Preserve the original claim and context while changing the format.

steps.title: Choose one useful takeaway
steps.description: Select a single supported point from the reviewed guide. Keep enough context to avoid changing its meaning.

artifact.title: Takeaway card
artifact.code:
Claim: a small first task includes manageable setup effort
Context: issue scope alone does not reveal onboarding effort
Example: a one-line fix can still require a complex local environment
Source: [reviewed guide URL]
Do not imply: every documentation task is easy

steps.title: Write for the destination
steps.description: Change length and structure to fit the channel while keeping the original point, its qualification, and its source.

artifact.title: Adaptation prompt
artifact.code:
Turn the takeaway card into a short contributor-newsletter item.
Keep the claim, the setup-effort caveat, and the guide link.
Use a practical opening and one clear next action.
Do not add statistics, endorsements, or promises.

steps.title: Compare with the source
steps.description: Review the adaptation beside the source card. A shorter version should still mean the same thing.
steps.checkpoint: The claim and qualification survive the format change.

artifact.title: Final comparison
artifact.code:
[ ] Original claim preserved
[ ] Important qualification retained
[ ] No new unsupported facts
[ ] Source link included
[ ] Next action fits the destination channel
